- Hair
- Hairline
- Hair color
- Facial proportions
- Body proportions
- Height
- Physique
- Skin tone
- Age appearance

Use one simple, clean, fitted outfit suitable for a professional character/model reference sheet.

The EXACT SAME outfit must appear in all 10 frames.

Do not change clothing between panels.

Do not change hairstyle between panels.

Minimal environment.

No scenery.

No props.

No dramatic background.

No unnecessary objects.

FACE FRAMES:
Head-and-shoulders framing.

FULL-BODY FRAMES:
Head-to-feet framing with the entire body completely visible.

Exactly 5 equal-width panels on the TOP ROW.

FRONT
3/4 LEFT
LEFT PROFILE

RIGHT PROFILE

3/4 LEFT

3/4 RIGHT
BACK

1. Front

4. 3/4 Right
5. Right Profile

AI video generation
Animation
Film production
Storyboarding
Character design
Fashion visualization
3D character development

EXACTLY 10 FRAMES ONLY.

No 8 frames.
No 9 frames.
No 11 frames.
No extra portraits.
No extra poses.
No additional panels.

No identity change.
No different person.
No face variation.

No gender change.

No hair color change.
No body-shape change.
No inconsistent clothing.
No inconsistent proportions.
No duplicated panels.
No missing panels.
No distorted profile.
No distorted hands.
No extra fingers.
No extra limbs.
No cropped feet in full-body frames.
No cropped head in face frames.

No cartoon style.

No plastic skin.

No watermark.

FINAL OUTPUT:
A single clean professional 2-row × 5-column character reference sheet containing EXACTLY 10 consistent views of the same person.

🎉 Five papers accepted at NeurIPS 2026!

Excited to share our work across protein design, RNA design and evaluation, efficient LLM agents, and multimodal safet
Here’s what we explored 👇

🧬 1 | Grounding protein generation in physics
<Equivariant Force Field Calibration for Flow-based Protein Design>

Generative models can produce protein structures quickly—but physical plausibility remains a critical challenge.

This work combines differentiable force-field guidance with consistency-based training to calibrate flow models toward low-energy, sterically valid conformations. Across full-atom generation and peptide binder modeling, we improve physical plausibility and geometric stability while enabling sampling with very few steps.

🧪 2 | Learning RNA design preferences from physical feedback
<Pareto Preference Optimization for Structure- and Stability-Aware RNA Inverse Folding>

RNA design requires satisfying several objectives together: structural fidelity, local accuracy, and thermodynamic stability. Optimizing one metric can create shortcuts that undermine the others.

We introduce RiboPO, a preference optimization framework that constructs preferences through Pareto comparisons, uses structural gates to guard against compositional reward hacking, and fine-tunes an RNA inverse-folding model using DPO.

📄 Earlier preprint:
https://t.co/vaCxwPzlid

💻 Code (anonymous review repository):
https://t.co/QGvWWAzJGt

🔍 3 | Testing whether RNA design scores deserve our trust
<Multi-Oracle Agreement Reveals the Limits of Self-Consistency Evaluation in RNA Design>

What happens when the predictor used to optimize a sequence is also used to evaluate it? Across approximately 11,000 RNA designs, we find that 78.1% of designs from single-objective optimization pass one predictor yet fail another. Ensemble-based methods reduce this disagreement substantially.

We introduce ACCORD, an evaluation workflow that combines independent predictors and calibrates their disagreement against experimental chemical-mapping data.

📄 Paper:
https://t.co/9aaIHcUNnj

💻 Code (anonymous review repository):
https://t.co/ABGhHfbEMd

⚡ 4 | Making LLM agents more efficient by changing how they act
<Latent Action Reparameterization for Efficient Agent Inference>

Agent inference cost depends on both the cost of each decision and the number of decisions required.

LAR learns compact, executable latent actions from recurring patterns in agent trajectories. This shortens the effective decision horizon, reducing action tokens and inference time while maintaining or improving task success across the evaluated benchmarks.

📄 Paper:
https://t.co/UneHr0ue8q
💻 Code:
https://t.co/Oq6qq9jxH6

🛡️ 5 | Understanding the safety implications of thinking with images
<When Think-with-Image Meets Safety: What Determines Multimodal Jailbreak Robustness?>

As vision-language models increasingly reason through visual operations and external tools, their inference pipelines become part of the safety question.

Across the evaluated models, explicit image-tool interaction reduces jailbreak success by around 30% relative on average. Representation analyses and activation interventions support an account in which tool invocation shifts hidden states toward a safety-relevant direction.

📄 Paper:
https://t.co/bCsVQQIS5E

Huge thanks to my coauthors, advisors, and collaborators for making this work possible!

**TL;DR:** This is a CIA-translated issue of a 1984 Chinese psychic-research magazine. Chinese scientists claimed kids could read with their ears and pull paper out of sealed envelopes using their minds. The CIA collected it because it was tracking foreign psychic research.

**What it is**
- A quarterly called *Research in Human Paranormal Capabilities* (Volume 2, published June 15, 1984), covering Chinese experiments on psychic abilities and Qigong
- It's in the CIA's STARGATE files, the US government's own psychic-spying program

**The origin story**
- On March 11, 1979, a Sichuan newspaper reported that a schoolboy named Tang Yu could read Chinese characters with his ear. Soon other kids around China were reported to have the same ability.
- China's researchers made that date the official birthday of "human science" and held anniversary parties nationwide

**The drama**
- Critics called the research anti-Marxist, "feudal sorcery," and said the researchers were idiots
- The psychic camp got a defense-industry official on their side, and in 1982 the Communist Party's propaganda department ruled the research could continue
- So it was settled by politics, not proof

**The wildest experiments**
- **Envelope trick:** A subject called "Z" supposedly wrote on paper inside a sealed envelope, pulled paper out of a sealed envelope, and put a photo into one, all without opening it
- **Needle trick:** A kid supposedly broke a needle inside a sealed matchbox with his mind, then fused it back together
- **Hand reading:** 25 kids "read" cards placed on an acupuncture point on the wrist. They said they felt tingling or heat traveling up the arm to the head, saw flashes, and then the image came into focus.
- **Inner microscope:** Adults getting acupuncture claimed they could see their own cells blown up to the size of beans

**Red flags**
- The "controls" were basically "we watched really closely"
- Even the leading scientist in the issue admitted Tang Yu had lost his powers and nobody had properly recorded his case
- Z often needed to wait hours before he could "perform", which gives a magician plenty of time
- None of these claims has ever held up under real scientific testing. Magicians can do every one of these tricks.

**Why it matters:** During the Cold War, the US worried that China and the USSR were ahead in psychic research. Documents like this one are part of why the US spent years funding its own psychic program.
